title: Propose a remedy for the history check failing on squash ee4b0dd
summary: I read this as a request for a written proposal on why main's history check fails after the multi-job squash merge ee4b0dd, with options and a recommendation recorded as a decision entry. It does not implement the fix.

defaults_applied.how: The remedy touches the gate, so it is written down with alternatives before anything is built.
Cause and options cite the gate code, design §7.3, and D60/D61.
One docs change; implementation is left to a follow-up job.
Recovered the history exemption mechanism and squash handling from the repository instead of asking.
Entry written for an outside reader, in the existing decision format.

assumptions: 'What do you propose?' asks for a written proposal, not an immediate fix, so the deliverable is a decision entry with options and a recommendation.

The history check fails because the landing check judges a squash as one job's landing, and ee4b0dd carries records of several jobs (read from design §7.3 and landing_tests.rs; the exact failure output was not available to me).
The full 40-character id of ee4b0dd is not available in the snapshot, so the proposal does not edit athena.toml.
Recommendation leans toward (b) or (a): exempting is cheap and low reversal-cost for this one commit, while (c) prevents recurrence; the producer should pick on evidence from the code.
question: Do you want just the written proposal, or also the fix (for example exempting ee4b0dd in athena.toml, or changing the landing check to accept multi-job squashes)?

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/decisions.md gains a new, next-numbered decision entry (Decision, Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal cost, Provenance) on the failing history check after the squash-merge of PR #8 (ee4b0dd, many job landings in one commit).

The entry names the cause with citations to the landing check in crates/athena-gate (and design §7.3), stating that a squash is judged as one landing of one job, so a commit carrying several jobs' records fails; claims cite files read or commands run.

The entry compares at least three options: (a) exempt ee4b0dd via [history] exempt (D60/D61, full 40-character id), (b) teach the landing check to accept a commit that lands several jobs when each job's records are complete, (c) stop squashing multi-job PRs (merge commit or rebase merge) and rewrite nothing; it recommends one and says why.

No file other than docs/decisions.md (and optionally CHANGELOG.md) changes; athena.toml, workflows and code are untouched, and the entry says implementation is a follow-up job awaiting the user's choice.
Run `cargo test` and `cargo clippy` from the repository root: both still pass (docs-only change; any test that checks decision numbering or docs still holds). `cargo fmt --check` is clean.

out_of_scope: Changing the landing-check code or tests.
Editing athena.toml to add an exemption.
departures: Docs-only proposal, so cost and time lean lower than the reference; but the user may want the fix implemented, which raises intervention and lowers acceptance.
